theme: Rep the 6ix without getting priced out of it

events.text: Okay, hot take: I think I finally understand Drake.
You've lived here six years and you just now got it?
No no, I always *liked* him. I mean I get the *job*. He's basically the city's hype man with a platinum record deal.
He put the CN Tower on an album cover and the whole world went 'ohhh it's a big needle.' We've been looking at that thing our whole lives.
I proposed to you under it. Well - I proposed on the lawn, and the Tower just sort of loomed. Very romantic looming.
Two double-doubles and a box of Timbits - twenty of them, and if you give me a single birthday-cake one I'm walking out.
She means it. We had a whole incident in 2021.
Anyway. The lineup's out the door because it's minus twelve and everyone discovered the drive-thru is somehow slower than walking.
That's the 6ix in one image: eight lanes of traffic, everyone still taking the streetcar.
Because the streetcar actually shows up, babe. Mostly.
It 'shows up' the way Drake 'shows up' at a Raptors game - eventually, and in a very nice coat.
Alan! Bridgette! You will not *believe* what the No Thrills on the corner is doing.
Kessler, we're just here for eggs.
Eggs, sure, but also - they've got a whole bin of 'Toronto-exclusive' hot sauce. It's just regular hot sauce with the CN Tower on it. Six ninety-nine!
So it's... the normal hot sauce, but it knows where it lives.
Exactly! You understand! I bought nine.
Why nine?
One for each million people who claim they were at that Raptors parade. Gotta go - my streetcar's coming, allegedly.
Okay, real talk. I love that song, I love the Tower, I love this dumb cold city. But I feel like a fraud repping the 6ix when my rent just went up again.
...yeah. The city's been gentrifying the *us* right out of it.
My parents' whole street used to be bakeries and a guy who fixed vacuums. Now it's a boutique that sells - I'm not kidding - artisanal ice for ten dollars.
The 6ix is a Drake album and a CN Tower and also a landlord who calls your apartment a 'junior one-bedroom.'
Still. We're here. We're repping. Even if we're repping from a slightly smaller square footage.
So I did a thing.
Oh no.
I got us custom licence plates. Official. 'T-H-E-6-I-X.' Because we're not leaving. We're just gonna be *here*, loudly, forever.
You spent money on this. In this economy.
Sixty dollars. And honestly? Worth it. Now every time we drive anywhere, the whole city knows we're repping it.
You don't own a car.
...They'll look great on the fridge.
They'll look great on the fridge. Come here, you absolute menace of a Torontonian.
